value.rationale: The square at all width budgets is a natural complete optimal partial plank covering problem. The exactly solvable two-branch area law has a genuine sharp rotation threshold at covered fraction 3/4, and the inverse answers the minimum width to reach a target area. The all-family weighted angular dispersion gap controls arbitrary near-extremizers and is not supplied by the existing existential one-plank theorem; the result is not a chosen isolated numerical example.
